concept_name: AC Voltage Applied to an Inductor
source_book: NCERT Class 12 Physics, Ch.7 Alternating Current, §7.3 AC Voltage Applied to an Inductor — table-of-contents reference only; teaching authored from first principles, no sequence/example/figure imported. Second of 8 in the founder-reordered Ch.7 map (ac_voltage_resistor -> ac_voltage_inductor -> ac_voltage_capacitor -> phasors -> series_lcr_circuit -> ac_power_factor -> lc_oscillations -> transformer; phasors now sits AFTER the three individual element concepts, so this diamond must stand entirely on time-domain reasoning -- no rotating-vector diagram appears anywhere). The atomic idea: a pure inductor's current lags its applied sinusoidal voltage by EXACTLY a quarter cycle (90 degrees) because voltage sets the current's SLOPE (v = L di/dt, the coil's own back-emf fighting every change) rather than its size, so the current is geometrically forced to crest exactly where the voltage vanishes; the opposition is frequency-made reactance Xl = omega*L (the same coil chokes fast AC harder than slow AC, unlike a resistor's fixed R); and the average power is EXACTLY zero -- every joule borrowed into the magnetic field during one quarter cycle is fully returned during the next, twice per cycle (the anti-resistor: opposition without consumption). SCOPE: the capacitor's mirror behaviour (deferred to ac_voltage_capacitor), the rotating-vector/phasor formalism (deferred to phasors -- the '1.0 s = quarter cycle = 90 degrees' bracket is the deliberate seed for that later formalization), inductor DC transients/LR time constants (already taught in the shipped inductance concept, callback only), and combining L with R and C (deferred to series_lcr_circuit). Conceptual-only (no mode_overrides), EPIC-L-first (no epic_c_branches; the three misconceptions -- 'voltage and current always move together', 'a component's opposition is fixed like resistance', and 'fighting the current all cycle must burn energy' -- are confronted inside EPIC-L via Rule 16a misconception_watch at exactly S2, S5, S7, each a straightforward contrast beat, no predict->reveal). Routed to the NEW field_3d 'ac_inductor' scenario -- a coil apparatus (not a heater) with cool blue-cyan breathing field loops, a back-emf arrow pair independently timed from the wire-current arrow (a deliberate 1.0s stagger that makes the lag mechanically visible), a dual-strip scope pane (a clock-drawn i-trace plus a static dashed in-phase 'ghost' hypothesis and a lag bracket), a SIGNED p-strip crossing zero, a tangent-walk cursor for the PRIMARY-aha state, a scripted closed-form f-ramp for the reactance state, a breathing U = half*L*i-squared stored-energy gauge, and a re-tasked avg_p meter held dead at 0.00 W -- built in-loop for this concept (docs/loop_runs/ch7_engine_log.md, Stage 2, commit 35ae566) as a CLEAN STANDALONE SIBLING of the sealed ac_resistor scenario (no acr_-prefixed code touched); renderer contract quoted verbatim from that engine-log handoff. entry_state_map's PRIMARY aha (S4, the voltage-sets-the-slope insight) sits INSIDE the foundational slice (S1-S4), so no mandatory exit-pill is required; optional cross-slice pills route foundational -> reactance (S5) -> power (S6-S7) -> derivation (S8). Every state is live (show_sliders true, Rule 31) but exposes only its own relevant control row(s): vm at S4 (plain live, no scripted driver), f_demo at S5 (scripted ramp + drag-seize + thumb-lockstep), ALL THREE (vm/f_demo/L) at S9 (explore). Frequency is deliberately LOCKED in S1-S4 -- unlike the sibling, dragging f here changes the current's amplitude and would pre-spoil S5's own reveal; the lock IS the lesson's shape. Handoff to ac_voltage_capacitor (next concept): this diamond ends with a time-domain lag bracket and no phasor arrow anywhere -- the capacitor sibling mirrors this exact arc (ghost-compare -> mechanism -> slope/lead -> reactance -> power slosh) for a cheap L<->C symmetry that series_lcr_circuit will exploit; no fix cycle on this concept may ever add a phasor arrow.

real_world_anchor.primary: Inside almost every two-way loudspeaker sits a plain coil of wire in front of the bass driver. It lets the drumbeat through and chokes the treble — the SAME coil, opposing different frequencies by different amounts, exactly Xₗ = ωL doing its job. And it does this without warming up: a resistor placed there would waste the music as heat; the coil merely borrows energy and hands it back, twice every cycle.
real_world_anchor.secondary: The choke — the current-limiting coil found in fluorescent-tube ballasts, LED drivers, and motor soft-starters. Engineers reach for a coil precisely when they need to hold AC current back WITHOUT paying the resistor's heat bill; the name 'choke' is the concept in one word. Mains frequency is phrased neutrally throughout — 'the mains frequency', never a fixed regional number.

f_demo.name: Demo-compressed AC frequency (real mains is tens of Hz)

theta.name: Instantaneous phase — native radians, state-local clock (Rule 26)
theta.derived: theta = omega * t   [EXCEPT S5 while undragged, which uses the closed-form ramp-phase accumulator of the S5 lemma in place of omega*t]

Xl.name: Inductive reactance — the coil's frequency-made opposition

i.name: Instantaneous current
i.derived: i = im * sin(theta - PI/2) = -im * cos(theta)   [lags v by exactly PI/2 rad = 90° = T/4, always]

slope_i.name: Instantaneous slope of the current — the S4 PRIMARY-aha value, the tangent-walk cursor's live number
slope_i.derived: slope_i = v / L   [exact at every instant — v = L di/dt rearranged; NEVER a hardcoded 3.14, since v (and hence slope_i) is live-draggable at S4]

eps_back.name: Back-emf induced across the coil's own turns (S3)
eps_back.derived: eps_back = -v   [Lenz: opposes the applied voltage volt-for-volt, at every instant, both while i rises AND falls]

p.name: Instantaneous power delivered TO the inductor (S6/S8) — SIGNED, unlike ac_voltage_resistor's p
p.derived: p = v * i = -(vm*im/2) * sin(2*theta)   [+ = storing into the field, − = field returning energy to the source]

p_avg.name: Cycle-average power — EXACT zero, over any interval as short as T/2 = π/ω (p's own period), not just a full T

U.name: Energy stored in the inductor's magnetic field, instantaneous — the U-gauge value
U.derived: U = 0.5 * L * i^2 = Umax * cos(theta)^2   [breathes 0 <-> Umax TWICE per source period T; dU/dt = p(t) exactly]

Umax.name: Maximum stored energy — the U-gauge's ceiling AND the p-strip store-lobe's shaded area

lag_seconds.name: Time lag between the v-peak and the i-peak — the S2 bracket's number

lag_degrees.name: Phase lag in degrees — frequency-INDEPENDENT, always exactly a quarter cycle

bead_frac.name: Micro-band wire-bead position fraction, 0/1=ends 0.5=home (Rule 33b)
bead_frac.derived: bead_frac = 0.5 - A_frac * sin(theta)   [beads are momentarily AT REST exactly when i=0 — i.e. at the v-PEAK instants — the S1 plant]

A_frac.name: Bead-excursion visual scale, calibrated to 0.30 at defaults

field_brightness.name: Coil field-loop brightness/density — cool blue-cyan geometry ONLY, the coil BODY never receives this or any emissive (Rule 33d)
field_brightness.derived: field_brightness = U/Umax = cos(theta)^2   [max exactly when i is at ITS OWN peak, i.e. at v=0 — the S1 plant; self-normalized to that state's own Umax]

arrow_dir.name: Wire-current arrow direction / field-loop circulation sense
arrow_dir.derived: arrow_dir = sign(i) = -sign(cos(theta))   [flips at i's zero crossings: t = T/4, 3T/4, ... i.e. AT THE v-PEAK instants — the OPPOSITE timing from ac_voltage_resistor's arrow, which flips at v-zero]

formulas.instantaneous_voltage: v = vₘ sin(ωt) — the applied AC voltage, ω = 2πf_demo
formulas.faraday_relation: v = L·(di/dt) — the defining law: voltage sets the current's SLOPE, not its size (S4 PRIMARY aha)
formulas.instantaneous_current: i = iₘ sin(ωt − 90°) = −iₘ cos(ωt), iₘ = vₘ/Xₗ — current lags voltage by exactly a quarter cycle
formulas.back_emf: ε_back = −v — the coil's induced emf opposes the applied voltage volt-for-volt at every instant (S3)
formulas.reactance: Xₗ = ωL — the frequency-made opposition; Xₗ→0 as ω→0 (a DC-steady inductor is an ideal short)
formulas.instantaneous_power: p = v·i = −(vₘiₘ/2) sin(2ωt) — SIGNED, symmetric about zero, twice the source frequency
formulas.average_power: ⟨p⟩ = 0 EXACTLY — not approximately — over any interval that is a whole multiple of T/2 = π/ω
formulas.stored_energy: U = ½Li² = Umax cos²(ωt), Umax = ½Liₘ² — breathes 0↔Umax twice per source period; dU/dt = p(t) exactly
formulas.lobe_area_link: ∫ p dt over any store quarter = Umax exactly
formulas.point_symmetry_fold: p(t_c+τ) = −p(t_c−τ) at ANY zero crossing t_c of p(t) — every positive lobe is the EXACT 180°-point-rotation of its trailing negative lobe about their shared zero crossing (S8's fold)
formulas.closed_form_derivation: v=L di/dt → i=−(vₘ/ωL)cos ωt = iₘ sin(ωt−π/2); the ω in the denominator IS Xₗ's frequency-dependence, and the −cos IS the 90° lag — one integration yields both headline results (S8)

constraints: i(t) = im sin(ωt − π/2) lags v(t) = vm sin(ωt) by EXACTLY π/2 rad (90°, T/4) at every instant — never leads, never in-phase, for a pure ideal inductor.
v = L di/dt exactly, at every instant — the SLOPE of i is what v sets, never i's value directly (this is the entire content of the PRIMARY aha).
Xl = ωL grows linearly with frequency; Xl → 0 as ω → 0 (an ideal short at steady DC — consistent with the shipped inductance concept's 'current never jumps').
p(t) = v(t)·i(t) = −(vm·im/2)·sin(2ωt) is exactly odd-symmetric about every one of its own zero crossings — store and return lobe areas cancel PAIRWISE and exactly, never approximately, so ⟨p⟩ = 0.
U(t) = ½Li(t)² ≥ 0 always; dU/dt = p(t) exactly — the U-gauge and the p-strip are the SAME physics, never independently scripted.
An ideal inductor has zero resistance — it dissipates NOTHING; every joule delivered to it over any quarter cycle is returned in the following quarter cycle exactly.

aha_moment.statement: Voltage sets the current's slope, not its size — the lag is pure geometry.
aha_moment.visual_confirmation: The tangent cursor steepens exactly at the voltage peak and goes flat exactly at the current's crest — the lag falls straight out of the slope relationship, not the coil's material.

STATE_1.title: Same source, new component: an ideal coil

scene_composition.text: same alternating source as before
charges pause exactly at the voltage peak
coil field swells brightest at zero voltage

tts_sentences.text_en: Same alternating source, but now it feeds a coil instead of a heater — everything still swings.
Watch the charges pause and turn exactly when the voltage peaks, not when it's zero.
The coil's field swells brightest exactly when the voltage crosses zero instead — hold that thought.

STATE_2.title: The current lags the voltage by a quarter cycle

scene_composition.text: dashed guess: a resistor's in-phase rhythm
real current sweeps in, arriving late
1.0 s = one quarter cycle = 90 degrees

tts_sentences.text_en: Here's what a resistor's current would do — the dashed guess, copying voltage instantly.
But this coil's charges won't obey — they pause where the guess claims maximum flow.
Watch the real current sweep in — same size, but arriving late.
It peaks a full quarter cycle after the voltage — ninety degrees behind, always.

misconception_watch.belief: Voltage and current always move together — Ohm's rhythm is universal.
misconception_watch.visual_counter: The dashed in-phase ghost trace docks first, the beads visibly disobey it, and the real current peaks a full quarter cycle later with the lag bracket confirming one quarter cycle equals ninety degrees.
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: Only the resistor is that obedient — a coil's current always runs a quarter-cycle behind.

STATE_3.title: The coil fights every change with an opposing back-emf

scene_composition.text: current rising: back voltage opposes it
current falling: back voltage flips to help
back voltage always equal and opposite

tts_sentences.text_en: Zoom into the coil: as current rises, its own field induces a back voltage opposing the rise.
As current falls, that back voltage flips — now it props the current up instead.
The back voltage always mirrors the source, equal and opposite — fighting the change, never the current itself.

STATE_4.title: Voltage sets the slope — the PRIMARY aha

scene_composition.text: voltage sets the slope, not the size
voltage at peak: current climbs steepest
voltage at zero: current crests, flat slope

tts_sentences.text_en: Here's the rule: voltage doesn't set the current's size, it sets its slope — how fast it's changing.
Where voltage peaks, the current climbs its steepest.
Where voltage is zero, the slope goes flat — exactly where the current crests.
Drag the peak voltage: every tangent steepens, but the crest never moves — pure geometry.

scene_composition.text: reactance equals angular frequency times inductance
faster swing: current shrinks
slower swing: current swells

tts_sentences.text_en: The coil's opposition isn't fixed like a resistor's — frequency makes it: reactance equals angular frequency times inductance.
Watch faster swings choke harder: current shrinks and the beads barely move before turning back.
Slow it back down and the current swells right back up.
Same trick lets a speaker coil pass bass, choke treble.

misconception_watch.belief: A component's opposition is a fixed property, like resistance.
misconception_watch.visual_counter: The same coil, nothing about it changed, quintuples its opposition as frequency ramps — the reactance readout climbs from 2.0 to 10.0 ohms while the peak current collapses from 5.0 to 1.0 amps.
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: A coil's opposition isn't built in — frequency makes it fresh: reactance equals angular frequency times inductance.

scene_composition.text: power equals voltage times current, every instant
same sign: storing — opposite sign: returning
shaded area equals the gauge's peak: 6.37 J

tts_sentences.text_en: Multiply voltage by current — power swings both positive and negative.
When they share a sign, power is positive — energy pours into the field, the gauge fills.
When they disagree, power turns negative — the field gives that energy back.
That shaded area equals what the gauge just filled — nothing lost.

STATE_7.title: Nothing is consumed — average power is exactly zero

scene_composition.text: average-power meter: dead at zero
current still flows, field still breathes
coil body: never warms

tts_sentences.text_en: Here's an averaging wattmeter — watch it stay dead at zero, cycle after cycle.
Current is clearly flowing, the field keeps breathing, and the gauge keeps filling and draining.
But the coil never warms — it borrows energy and hands back every joule; only resistance actually eats it.

misconception_watch.belief: The coil fights the current all cycle, so it must be burning energy — reactance heats like resistance.
misconception_watch.visual_counter: The wattmeter needle stays dead at 0.00 watts while peak current visibly flows and the coil body stays cold, unlike the resistor's steady 10.0 watt glow on the same source.
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: Reactance stores and returns; only resistance eats.

scene_composition.text: one integration of voltage equals inductance times rate of current change
out falls both the 90-degree lag and the reactance
each power lobe rotates onto the next — average exactly zero

tts_sentences.text_en: Nothing moves here — just one integration of voltage equals inductance times current's rate of change.
Out falls a negative cosine — the quarter-cycle lag — with angular frequency times inductance beneath it, the reactance.
The power curve folds exactly: each lobe rotates a half turn onto the next, canceling pair by pair.

STATE_9.title: Explore — the whole inductor circuit, live

scene_composition.text: drag peak voltage, frequency, inductance
watch the lag, the field, the current respond live
current lags voltage by one quarter cycle (90 degrees)

tts_sentences.text_en: It's all yours now — drag peak voltage, frequency, and inductance, and watch the lag, the field, and the current respond live.

assessment.mastery_definition: A student has mastered AC voltage on an inductor when they can (1) state that a pure inductor's current lags its applied sinusoidal voltage by exactly a quarter cycle (90 degrees), never leads and is never in phase; (2) explain WHY the lag exists — the coil's own changing flux induces a back-emf that opposes the change, so the applied voltage sets the current's SLOPE (v = L di/dt) rather than its instantaneous size; (3) read off the current's instantaneous behaviour at any point in the voltage cycle — zero and changing steepest where voltage peaks, at its own peak where voltage is zero; (4) compute the peak current from the reactance, im = vm/Xl with Xl = omega*L, and predict how doubling the frequency (or the inductance) changes it; (5) state that the cycle-average power delivered to a pure inductor is exactly zero, and explain where the energy goes — stored in the magnetic field, then fully returned; (6) contrast reactance with resistance — a coil opposes current without ever dissipating energy, unlike a resistor; and (7) derive, from v = L di/dt, both the 90-degree lag and the reactance Xl = omega*L in one integration, and show that the resulting power p = v*i averages to exactly zero.

questions.stem: A pure inductor (near-zero resistance) carries a sinusoidal AC voltage. Compared to the voltage, how does the current behave?

options.A: The current peaks exactly a quarter cycle (90°) AFTER the voltage — it lags
options.B: The current peaks exactly a quarter cycle (90°) BEFORE the voltage — it leads
options.C: The current peaks at exactly the same instant as the voltage — zero phase difference
options.D: The current and voltage have no fixed timing relationship — it depends on the resistor value

distractor_misconceptions.B: imports the capacitor's lead behaviour (a later sibling concept) onto an inductor
distractor_misconceptions.C: imports the resistor's in-phase rhythm — the exact prior belief this concept confronts
distractor_misconceptions.D: misses that an ideal (near-zero-resistance) inductor has no resistor value governing the timing — the lag is fixed at exactly 90° by the coil's own geometry

questions.tested_idea: For a pure inductor, current lags voltage by exactly a quarter cycle (90°) — never leads, never in phase.
questions.parallel_form_stem: A student says an inductor's current 'copies the voltage but a bit late.' State the exact phase relationship, in degrees, and name which quantity is ahead.

questions.stem: WHY does an inductor's current lag its voltage by exactly a quarter cycle?

options.A: The coil's own changing flux induces a back-voltage that opposes the change, so the applied voltage only ever controls how FAST the current is changing — its slope — never its instantaneous size
options.B: The coil physically slows the electrons down as they travel through its turns
options.C: The coil stores charge like a capacitor and releases it later
options.D: The lag is just how AC works, no different from a plain wire

distractor_misconceptions.B: invents a mechanical electron-slowing mechanism with no physical basis — inductors don't impede electron speed
distractor_misconceptions.C: confuses an inductor's field-energy storage with a capacitor's charge storage — different mechanism, different physics
distractor_misconceptions.D: denies the coil-specific mechanism entirely, missing that a plain wire (near-zero inductance) shows no lag at all

questions.tested_idea: The lag exists because the coil's induced back-emf makes voltage set the current's SLOPE, not its size.
questions.parallel_form_stem: Explain in one sentence why an inductor's current can't simply track the applied voltage the way a resistor's does.

questions.stem: At the exact instant a pure inductor's voltage is at its POSITIVE PEAK, what is happening to the current?

options.A: The current is exactly zero, but changing at its fastest rate — climbing through zero at its steepest slope
options.B: The current is also at its positive peak
options.C: The current is at its negative peak
options.D: The current cannot be determined without knowing the resistance

distractor_misconceptions.B: imports the resistor's in-phase behaviour onto an inductor
distractor_misconceptions.C: confuses 'voltage at peak' with 'current at peak' — the two peaks are a quarter cycle apart, not opposite
distractor_misconceptions.D: misses that for a pure inductor the current's value depends only on inductance and frequency, not on any resistance

questions.tested_idea: Voltage sets the SLOPE of the current: at voltage's peak, current is zero but changing steepest; at voltage's zero, current is at its own peak.
questions.parallel_form_stem: At the instant a pure inductor's voltage crosses zero, what is true of the current at that same instant?

questions.stem: A pure inductor's peak current is im = vm/(omega*L). If the frequency of the applied AC is doubled (voltage amplitude and inductance unchanged), what happens to the peak current?

options.A: It halves — the reactance doubles, so the same peak voltage drives half the peak current
options.B: It doubles — a faster swing should drive more current
options.C: It stays the same — frequency doesn't affect a pure inductor
options.D: It quadruples — reactance depends on frequency squared

distractor_misconceptions.B: assumes 'faster' means 'more current,' the opposite of how reactance actually works
distractor_misconceptions.C: the confronted misconception — believes a component's opposition is a fixed property, missing that reactance is frequency-made
distractor_misconceptions.D: misremembers the reactance formula as frequency-squared rather than linear in frequency

questions.tested_idea: Reactance Xl = omega*L grows linearly with frequency, so peak current im = vm/Xl shrinks as frequency rises.
questions.parallel_form_stem: A coil chokes a 0.5 Hz signal to 1.0 A peak. Using the same coil and voltage, estimate the peak current at 0.1 Hz, and explain the trend.

questions.stem: A pure inductor carries AC continuously. What is its average power consumption over a full cycle, and where does the energy delivered during part of the cycle go?

options.A: Average power is exactly zero — every joule stored in the magnetic field during one quarter cycle is returned to the source during the next
options.B: Average power is exactly zero because no current is actually flowing
options.C: Average power is positive but small, since the coil has some resistance
options.D: Average power equals the peak instantaneous power, since current is always flowing somewhere in the circuit

distractor_misconceptions.B: confuses 'zero average power' with 'zero current' — current visibly flows at up to its peak value the whole time
distractor_misconceptions.C: imports resistive heating onto an IDEAL inductor, which by definition has zero resistance
distractor_misconceptions.D: confuses average power with peak power — very different numbers

questions.tested_idea: A pure inductor's average power is EXACTLY zero — energy is stored in the field and fully returned, never dissipated.
questions.parallel_form_stem: A wattmeter reads a steady 0.00 W on a coil while an ammeter shows 2.00 A of current flowing. Explain how both readings can be true at once.

questions.stem: Starting from v = L(di/dt) for a pure inductor with v = vm*sin(omega*t), which pair of results falls out of ONE integration?

options.A: i = im*sin(omega*t − pi/2), where im = vm/(omega*L) — the 90° lag AND the reactance omega*L both appear in the same expression
options.B: i = im*sin(omega*t), with no phase shift at all
options.C: i = im*cos(omega*t), with the reactance appearing as omega*L squared in the denominator
options.D: i = im*sin(omega*t + pi/2), leading the voltage by 90°

distractor_misconceptions.B: drops the phase shift entirely — imports the resistor's in-phase result
distractor_misconceptions.C: misremembers reactance as omega*L squared rather than the linear omega*L that the integration actually produces
distractor_misconceptions.D: gets the SIGN of the phase shift backwards — a lag, not a lead (that's the capacitor's later result)

questions.tested_idea: One integration of v = L di/dt yields both the 90° lag (the −cos term) and the reactance omega*L (the denominator) together.
questions.parallel_form_stem: Starting from v = L di/dt, derive the expression for instantaneous power p(t) and show that its cycle-average is exactly zero.
